newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index storms to record close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index storms to record close.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index stormed to record highs on Wednesday, as banking and property stocks shot up on expectations of a slew of warrant issues and after U.S. economic data soothed interest rate jitters.
The blue chip index posted its third biggest point gain ever, surging 472.78 points, or 3.56 percent, to a record close of 13,766.65. It hit an intra-day record high of 13,771.54.

"I think a number of firms are going to issue covered warrants particularly on banking and property stocks, and market sentiment was boosted by U.S. economic data released overnight," said Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities.
The high prices paid for two sites at the government's first land auction of the year also boosted sentiment in the property sector, he said.
A 2,008-square-metre site in Repulse Bay on the south side of Hong Kong island fetched HK$230 million compared with analysts forecasts of between HK$179 million and HK$188 million.
A 5,080-square-metre site in Tuen Mun in the New Territories sold for HK$258 million compared with forecasts of HK$178 million to HK$200 million.
Wednesday's turnover was HK$14.17 billion compared with HK$11.85 billion on Tuesday.

"We have seen a lot of fresh cash come in from both overseas institutions, local institutions as well as a lot of retail activity," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities. "I think there is every chance 14,500 will be seen in the first quarter."
Strong gains in U.S. stocks and bonds overnight following a benign U.S. December consumer price report had given the market an initial boost on Wednesday.

Interest rate sensitive banking and property stocks led Wednesday's surge. HSBC Holdings climbed HK$8.50 to HK$179.00 after reaching an all-time high of HK$180.00 during the session. Analysts said they expected HSBC to post strong earnings growth when it releases its final results on March 3.
"We think that even at this price level HSBC is still seriously undervalued," said Chan, adding that the stock could climb to HK$196 by the time earnings are released.
Hang Seng Bank jumped HK$2.75 to HK$96.25 and Bank of East Asia rose HK$1.30 to HK$37.30.
In the property sector, Cheung Kong surged HK$5.00 to HK$77.50, Sun Hung Kai Properties advanced HK$4.00 to HK$95.00 and New World Development gained HK$3.00 to HK$53.00.
